digests.headline: MacPhee poached, Lacroix through the door — Alonso's Chelsea is taking shape
digests.yesterday: The window did the work while nobody was watching. Chelsea triggered Austin MacPhee's release clause at Aston Villa — the set-piece coach whose dead-ball routines out-scored everyone in Europe's top five leagues in 2023-24 — and reporters covering Villa say he has already said his goodbyes there. Maxence Lacroix completed his medical in London, the £52m deal due to be wrapped up this week per Romano, while Como's third bid for Trevoh Chalobah, around £26m, has those talks accelerating into the weekend. One housekeeping note: our results feed was down today (the data provider returned errors on every request), so the usual scores, table and fixtures are missing from this page — though with the club mid-pre-season, there was mercifully little to miss.
digests.today: One month from today, Xabi Alonso takes charge of his first Premier League match, away to Fulham — the countdown post is already up on the club subreddit. Between now and then: a pre-season tour whose travelling squad includes 16-year-old Mahdi Nicoll-Jazuli, and one genuinely live negotiation, Leverkusen's Kerim Alajbegović, where Romano insists there is no £34m bid and Chelsea won't go much past €28m while Italian clubs circle. The honest read: this squad is already heavy, and The Standard reckons formalising the Alajbegović interest means selling Pedro Neto or loaning out Gittens first. Watch the sales, not the signings.

wider.title: Chelsea in talks for Villa set-piece guru MacPhee
wider.hook: Villa scored more set-piece goals than anyone in Europe's top five leagues under MacPhee in 2023-24. Chelsea just moved for the man responsible — the quiet hire that might matter more than a signing.

read.title: Chelsea paid Aston Villa £117m for Morgan Rogers. Is he the right fit?
read.hook: £117m makes Rogers the most expensive British player ever — and the numbers say he thrives galloping into space that Alonso's slow-build teams don't usually leave. That tension is the season's first tactical question.
